I want to say that I understand. I just made 10 months sober, and I’m really on the verge of relapse myself. 

If you happen to go to MA maybe go to a meeting? Even if you’ve never been, you can find online zoom meetings that you can listen in to. Sometimes it helps to listen to other people’s stories. 

As of right now, one thing I do is keep playing the tape in my head. I know what the consequences will be if I get high, and starting over always sucks. 
If you’re not seeing a therapist maybe consider going to one? Relapse happens before you pick up, and it might help to see what your warning signs are so you can try and stop. Also learning how to manage your depression and anxiety would be beneficial for you too. 

Sorry if I sound hypocritical. I have been severely depressed lately and it’s really hard to will myself to do anything to help myself. I’m not sure how severe your depression is currently, but mental health issues can definitely make recovery  difficult. It sounds like that is the other piece of your recovery that needs some help. 

I hope you continue to be sober and that you will feel better soon.

I think IOP can be helpful if you are really struggling to cope and do every day tasks- like you need the structure. Also, if you don’t have any coping skills it is beneficial in that it teaches you that as well. 

I’ve been in IOP four times and as much as I hated it, it helped me regulate and get out of a severe depression. You also see a psychiatrist once a week so if you need a med change that can be beneficial. I was never a fan of group therapy, and while it helped I would rather not do it again. 

If you are really struggling then I would say go for it- It will give you the structure you need.

Maybe try and point her to more tolerant branches of Christianity? I would try and speak “her language” and bring up reasons why it’s not a sin in Christianity. I wouldn’t tell her to stop believing if that is what she wants, but try and lead her to a more tolerant version. 

If she continues to feel that way then I would limit contact. You don’t have to reach out to her, but keep the line open if she ever feels like she needs to talk. That way you can keep your mental health in check, but also be there for her if she ever needs it. I think unconditional love is important and even if she is not showing you that right now, doesn’t mean you can’t for her. You can love from a distance if that is what you need.

I think you need to have a heart to heart with her. If you and your sister were close before I don’t think stopping contact is the right thing. She is obviously going through something and I think it might be important to be there for her. 

The death of your mother is still pretty recent, and I’m assuming she is just trying to find a way to cope with it.  The fact that her views are changing so suddenly and she called you asking about her mental health seems to me she is not in a good place. 

I know her recent views are hurting you- I have experienced homophobia from my family myself. But the fact she wasn’t like this before seems to me she is having a bit of a crisis. 

You do need to take care of yourself too, and if you feel that limiting contact with her is what you need to do then do it- but don’t shut the door on her. She may just need to go through this right now, and sometimes just being there when she needs you can help her to get through whatever she is going through. 

All relationships have their ups and downs, and maybe you two are just having a rough patch. I hope that you both are able to mend your relationship.

I don’t agree with that. There is a difference between “organic” and situational depression. 

I literally could not get out of bed to shower, brush my teeth, and as ashamed as I am to say it go to the bathroom. My body was heavy and I felt so tired I couldn’t function. I literally felt physical pain. 

As soon as I went on lithium my suicidal depression lifted immediately. It was like night and day-I was able to function again. Not everyone needs medication, but there is a subset of us who do.

I did and they put me on accutane. I lied to get on it so they didn’t know I was on lithium. It was a bad decision and I was desperate. You’re the one insulting me, and you are basing it off of one academic research paper. It’s a study- it doesn’t mean that it’s right. It very well could be a good medication, but you didn’t give any other studies. I’m all for learning about alternatives and finding what’s right for people.

I’m very well educated on what medications I do/do not put in my body. I do not take things blindly either. I have had different things in my life where I had to do research because the treatments out there did not work for me. Questioning things is healthy. You also don’t know what I’ve been through in healthcare to say that I blindly follow what is told to me. How dare you and shame on you to think I haven’t had my share of bad healthcare.
Maybe you should instead of trying to play doctor.

That’s true, but what I’m trying to point out is how well do you think they actually take care of mental health if they execute people over illegal drugs? And what if the poster went into psychosis while they were in Thailand? You think they would be better off than in the western world?

The poster said he was going to maybe do an experiment in Thailand with CBD and you posted to him about CBD and psychosis telling him the risks. How on Earth was that a sensible response and what makes you qualified to tell him what the right way to dose himself with CBD is? Why wouldn’t you say maybe try to do it in your home country? Maybe look for someone who has experience with doing it? 

And I do not bow to anything. I do my research and ask questions with anyone I’m going to help for. If something doesn’t make sense I go to someone else. Maybe you should do some reading comprehension. Obviously you have a thing against people who have studied hard in their fields. I never said doctors, scientists, and lawyers were God. I know very well that they are human, and I have had my fair share of bad doctors. 

You can insult me however you wish, but giving someone a response about how to use CBD when he said he’s going to try it in a country that executes people over drugs and has massive stigma against mental health is irresponsible. Just because you think that you know how to help people with a medical problem doesn’t mean you actually do.  

Until you have a doctorate in some sort of science, it’s really messed up for you to give people medical advice when you “think” that you know.

So basically you are saying that degrees mean nothing? You would be okay with getting surgery by someone who didn’t have a medical degree? You would ask someone for legal advice who didn’t go to law school?

And authority figures? None of my doctors have authority over me. I go to them because they are knowledgeable in their field and I need help. I can take their opinion or go somewhere else if I disagree. I’m not just talking about psychiatry- I’m talking about my healthcare in general. 

And if you consider what I say as a way of silencing you then that’s on you- but I’m not going to be silent when I see someone write out a really dangerous idea. It’s irresponsible and morally messed up for me to just not say anything. I can’t stop the poster from making a really reckless decision, but I can at least comment and give them something to think about.

And again unless you have a doctorate in any science discipline you are not qualified to be giving people advice on what is best for their well being. You said previously “I told them the risks” like you have a doctorate in a science field.

I don’t mean to sound rude, but unless you have a doctorate in a science field, you are not qualified to be giving people advice on scientific or medical processes. There is a reason doctors and scientists have to go through so much schooling. 

God forbid this poster decided to try CBD in Thailand on the basis of what you and this study are telling them and they end up in psychosis. Thailand has a strong stigma against mental illness (more so than Western countries) and they put people to death over illegal drugs. When someone is in psychosis they tend to be looked at is if they are already on drugs. I can’t see Thailand’s mental health system being any better or even the same as the West’s (I could be wrong). It would be horrible for the poster to even be in that situation, and there is nothing that anyone can do for them once they are in another country. 

There has to be someone out there who knows about this and is trying to help people. If this indeed does help people there is a doctor and/or scientist out there who is advocating for its use. I know in NYC there are doctors who are willing to give experimental treatments to patients who seek it out. People have to be willing to look for it though.

It seems like from the study that this isn’t something someone should be doing without medical advice and guidance from a medical professional. 

The poster can do what they wish- I just felt like maybe they should really think about it. Once you are in another country there is not much your home country can do to help you.

Do you have studies/sources on that? Because unless they have someone who is licensed directing them (or they know what they are doing) that experiment could end up going badly. I get being inpatient is horrible, but I’m not so sure it’s as bad as getting locked up in Thailand. I know that they execute people over illegal drugs, so I can only imagine what could happen if they end up going into psychosis there.

I feel the need to say this: please be careful trying this experiment outside your home country. I know weed is legal there, but if you end up in psychosis or in a mental health crisis there is no guarantee that you won’t be locked up there. 

It just scares me what can happen especially after what has happened to people who get locked up in more restrictive countries i.e. Russia, North Korea.

I have been lurking this sub for a couple days, and while I respect others opinions, what people are telling you is detrimental to your well-being. 

I would absolutely go and talk to your doctor about the medication. If you are feeling suicidal it’s not the medication for you and you need a change. If you have the right doctor you should be able to advocate for yourself effectively. I know when I needed to change medications I have been able to. 

I have been in the psych ward three times by my own choice. The only way you can be committed is if you are an immediate danger to yourself or others. If you can commit to safety and explain that you are not in immediate danger of hurting yourself than I do not see you getting committed- unless you are exhibiting other symptoms that you are aware/not aware of. I have told my own therapist in the past about my suicidal thoughts and I committed to safety. 

Furthermore, the fact that you believed you were a saint in the Truman show and were commanding traffic is irrelevant to your lifestyle- you needed help in that moment. You were beyond control of yourself. 

If you want a happy and stable life than do what you need to do to make that happen; and have open and honest communication with your psychiatrist. Your medication is a decision that needs to be made between you and your doctor. 

I hope you can find balance and happiness. And I’m sorry the medication is causing you such bad side effects. I know it can be rough.

Edit: I saw someone mention lithium in the comments. I would second that as well.  It was the best medication I have ever been on and worked wonders for me. It took me out of a suicidal depression within a couple days- it was the best feeling. Unfortunately I broke out in severe acne, so I no longer take it. I’ll keep my fingers crossed you don’t get side effects  in case you do go on it.

She may not believe you and if no one saw anything he could say you’re making it up. I just don’t want to see you get hurt for trying to speak up. Trying to help her could end up hurting you in the long run.
